title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 70
paragraphs: Such, then, was the commander of the Ethiopians above Egypt and of the Arabians — namely Arsames. But the Ethiopians from the direction of the sunrise (for the Ethiopians were in two contingents) had been assigned to serve with the Indians, differing from the other Ethiopians in no way except in their language and in the nature of their hair: the eastern Ethiopians have straight hair, while those of Libya have hair more thickly curled than any other men's. These Asian Ethiopians were armed for the most part like the Indians, but on their heads they wore the skin of a horse's forehead, flayed off together with the ears and mane, the mane serving as a crest, while the ears were set up straight and stiff. In place of shields they used protections of crane-skin held in front of them.
